trap-negation-contrast.evidence: table( pure-data block, 6 rows (atom, n strands, p(n), l(K,q_0), speedup). RECOMPUTED: p(3)=3, p(6)=11, p(9)=30, p(12)=77 -- all four partition counts correct. Strand counts consistent at 3 per nucleon (p/n 3, deuteron 6, triton/3He 9, 4He 12). The l column is exactly n-1 in every row (2,5,8,11), and Speedup = p(n)/l reproduces 3/2=1.5, 11/5=2.2, 77/11=7.0 exactly.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: ANOMALY (minor, arithmetic): the two 9-strand rows print Speedup 3.7x but 30/8 = 3.75, which rounds to 3.8 at one decimal -- the value is truncated, not rounded, and the neighbouring 7.0 row is exact, so the table is internally inconsistent about its rounding rule. Proposed fix: print 3.8x (or give 3.75x). Second note: the column is headed l(K,q_0), i.e. q_0-dependent, but every entry equals n-1 with no q_0 sensitivity shown and no witness cited; the parent prop:graded-hecke-energy-truncation-bound defines l as 'the confinement level at q_0' without supplying its value, so the column is unprovenanced as printed.
